idiom_name: interface with default bodies (and companion/object) instead of an empty base
implementation_notes: Kotlin interfaces may carry default implementations and still add no per-instance storage to implementing classes, so a stateless policy is an interface (or a companion object), not an empty base class; extension functions attach behaviour statically with no instance slot at all. The trap is class delegation: `class C(d: D) : I by d` compiles to a synthetic private backing field holding the delegate plus forwarding methods, so delegating to a stateless object still costs one reference per instance. Prefer interface default bodies when the behaviour is stateless; keep `by` for genuinely stateful composition, where the delegate is a real collaborator.
code_sketch:
interface Clock {                              // default body: no storage in implementors
    fun now(): Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
}

class Job : Clock                              // Job gains now() with no extra field

class WithDelegate(d: Clock) : Clock by d      // costs one synthetic delegate field

fun String.shout(): String = uppercase()       // extension: static dispatch, no storage
pitfalls: Interface delegation generates a private $$delegate_0 field per delegate, so a stateless delegate is not free - do not reach for `by` to avoid an empty base.

An abstract interface val still requires each implementation to supply an accessor, but it need not store state; a concrete implementation property with a backing field does, whereas a default getter adds none.
object and companion-object singletons are shared across the program, so they must not hold per-instance or per-request mutable state without synchronization.
